stage: one whose self is yoked in the yoga of Brahman
description: The happiness found in the self by one unattached to external contacts; with the self yoked in the yoga of Brahman he enjoys imperishable happiness (akṣaya sukha) — contrasted with contact-born enjoyments, which have a beginning and an end (5.22).

stage: the yogin who has become Brahman (brahmabhūta)
description: Happiness within (antaḥsukha), delight within (antarārāma) and light within (antarjyotis): the yogin who has these, having become Brahman, attains brahma-nirvāṇa.

stage: the calmed, stainless yogin who has become Brahman
description: The highest happiness (sukham uttamam) that comes to the yogin whose mind is calmed and whose rajas is stilled, who has become Brahman and is stainless; always yoking himself he easily attains the boundless happiness of contact with Brahman (brahma-saṃsparśa).

description: Arjuna's difficulty: the mind is restless, turbulent, strong and obstinate, as hard to hold as the wind, so the yoga of sameness does not seem able to stand steady (6.33–34); Kṛṣṇa grants this and names practice and dispassion as the means (6.35).

stage: yogabhraṣṭa (one fallen from yoga), in a new birth
description: Reborn among the pure or among yogins, the one fallen from yoga regains the connection with understanding of his former body and strives again; he is carried along by his former practice even without his will (6.43–44).

description: By knowledge one sees all beings in the self and then in the Lord (4.35); the yogin yoked in yoga, seeing the same everywhere, sees the self in all beings and all beings in the self (6.29); whoever sees the Lord everywhere and everything in him is never lost to him (6.30); established in oneness he worships the Lord as abiding in all beings (6.31).

stage: the yogin whose mind (citta) is stilled by the practice of yoga
description: The state called yoga: the mind (citta) stilled (niruddha) by practice comes to rest; seeing the self by the self one is content in the self; one knows boundless (ātyantika) happiness grasped by the intellect and beyond the senses, and established in it does not waver from the truth; having gained it one counts no other gain greater, and is not shaken even by heavy sorrow; it is the disconnection from union with suffering.

stage: the yogin of restrained mind (citta) practising the yoga of the self
description: The simile handed down for the yogin of restrained mind (yata-citta): a lamp in a windless place that does not flicker.
